import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN Source3_32_2 and Source3_32_1 on movie_id
df21 = pd.merge(df2, df1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# 2) JOIN Source3_32_0 and the result of previous join on user_id
df_final = pd.merge(df0, df21, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema:
# Target Schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Convert columns to required types:
# - title: string (already string)
# - user_id: float
# - movie_id: integer
# - rating: float
# - timestamp: float
# - age: float
# - occupation: float

# Ensure movie_id is integer (it should be already, but enforce)
df_final["movie_id"] = df_final["movie_id"].astype(int)

# Convert user_id, age, occupation, rating, timestamp to float
df_final["user_id"] = df_final["user_id"].astype(float)
df_final["age"] = df_final["age"].astype(float)
df_final["occupation"] = df_final["occupation"].astype(float)
df_final["rating"] = df_final["rating"].astype(float)
df_final["timestamp"] = df_final["timestamp"].astype(float)

# Select columns in target order
df_target = df_final[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 and the above join on user_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that can serve as keys:
# title (string), user_id (float but unique id), movie_id (int), timestamp (float)
# We exclude float columns age and occupation from group by and aggregate them by mean
grouped = joined_all.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "timestamp"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write output
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_32/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
